summary.one_liner: CrowdSec is an open-source, participative security engine that detects malicious behavior from logs and HTTP requests, blocks attacking IPs, and shares threat data through a community blocklist.
summary.what_it_does: The Security Engine acts as an all-in-one IDS/IPS and WAF, analyzing log sources and HTTP requests to detect bad behavior. Active remediation is handled by separate Remediation Components placed at firewalls, reverse proxies, or CDNs, so detection and blocking can run on different machines. Attacks reported by users feed a community blocklist, which the engine uses to proactively block known malicious IPs. The AppSec component is described as a WAF built on Coraza that loads SecLang rules and the OWASP Core Rule Set, plus a YAML rule format. It can also issue JavaScript proof-of-work challenges to suspicious requests to stop headless browsers and scrapers while letting verified crawlers through. Scenarios for brute force, port scans and web scans ship by default, and more can be picked from the Hub. The README also mentions an optional Console for monitoring and management.
use_cases: block brute force attacks on servers
analyze logs from multiple sources in one place
web application firewall for HTTP requests
how_to_run: Follow the official documentation to install CrowdSec on Linux, Windows, Docker, OPNsense, Kubernetes, or other platforms.
notable: Detect here, remediate there: detection and blocking are decoupled across machines
Crowdsourced community blocklist built from shared attack reports
AppSec WAF built on Coraza that accepts SecLang and OWASP CRS rules
Proof-of-work JavaScript challenges for bot and scraper detection
Detection rules published on the Hub under MIT license
caveats: The README does not give the exact install or run commands; it points to external documentation.
Console features such as premium blocklists and advanced management are described as extras, with some premium features mentioned.
